stem.text: The function \( y = f(t) \) is a solution to the differential equation \( \frac{dy}{dt} = \left(t - 5\right) \left(t + 3\right) \left(- y - 1\right) \), and \( y < -1 \) for all t. For \( t > 0 \), find the input at which f has a critical point and determine whether it is the location of a relative minimum, a relative maximum, or neither.

answer_key.label: The solution has a relative minimum at \( t = 5 \), because the derivative changes from negative to positive at \( t = 5 \).

worked_solution.text: A critical point needs \( \frac{dy}{dt} = 0 \). Because \( y < -1 \), the factor \( y + 1 \) is never 0, and for \( t > 0 \) the factor \( t + 3 \) is positive, so the only zero in the range is \( t = 5 \).
worked_solution.rule_named: zeros of the right side within the stated range

worked_solution.text: On the range, the sign of \( \frac{dy}{dt} \) is the sign of \( \left(t - 5\right) \) times a positive quantity, so it is negative just before \( t = 5 \) and positive just after.
Because the derivative changes from negative to positive at \( t = 5 \), f has a relative minimum there.

options.label: The solution has a relative minimum at \( t = 5 \) and a relative maximum at \( t = -3 \), because the derivative changes sign at both inputs.
options.derivation: the zero at t = -3, outside the stated range, kept as a second critical point

options.label: The solution has a relative maximum at \( t = 5 \), because the derivative changes from negative to positive at \( t = 5 \).
options.derivation: the sign change found correctly and then read the wrong way round
